summary: This note lists the member countries of NATO, which has 29 members: two in North America (Canada and the United States), 27 European countries, and Turkey, which lies in Eurasia. It describes the military make-up of members, notes that Iceland has no typical army, and identifies the three nuclear weapons states. It also traces the timeline of expansion from the 12 original founders through later additions, including 13 after the Cold War.
one_line: Overview of NATO's 29 member countries, their geography, military capabilities, nuclear status, and membership expansion timeline.
key_facts: Two NATO members are located in North America: Canada and the United States.
27 NATO member countries are European countries.
Turkey is the NATO member located in Eurasia.
All NATO members have militaries except Iceland, which does not have a typical army.
Iceland has a coast guard and a small unit of civilian specialists for NATO operations.
France, the United Kingdom, and the United States are the three NATO members that are nuclear weapons states.
NATO had 12 original founding member nation states.
From 18 February 1952 to 6 May 1955, NATO added three more member nations.
NATO added a fourth member nation on 30 May 1982.
After the end of the Cold War, NATO added 13 more member nations from 12 March 1999 to 5 June 2017.
The 13 post-Cold War members comprised 10 former Warsaw Pact members and three former Yugoslav republics.
